headlines.text: Rewind to 2022, when the AEW World Heavyweight Title was up for grabs as Adam Page vs. Bryan Danielson went to war, appearing on Dynamite, rated 9.40 ? the kind of match that redefines a wrestler's career. Marking AEW Dynamite's debut on TBS, this was the rematch to their legendary 60-minute draw two weeks earlier, and it more than lived up to the billing ? both men were busted open bloody before Page finally retained with the Buckshot Lariat, in a match many later ranked among the best of the entire year.
Turning the clock back to 2024: The Butcher stepped back through the curtain after 3 months away, appearing on Rampage.

2022 brought us this moment: the AEW TBS Title made its debut as Jade Cargill vs. Ruby Soho battled for the honor of being first champion, appearing on Dynamite, rated 3.51. Also on AEW's first night on TBS, this was the final of the inaugural TBS Championship Tournament, capping a run that saw the undefeated Cargill and the battle-tested Soho both fight through a full bracket ? Cargill sealed history with an avalanche Jaded to become the first-ever champion.

secondaries.text: Looking back to 2022, when gold changed shoulders as the AEW World Tag Team Titles found a new champion as Jurassic Express vs. The Lucha Brothers battled it out, appearing on Dynamite, rated 7.31 ? a solid showing ? ending the champion's reign at 3 defenses. Closing out AEW's TBS premiere alongside the Page-Danielson main event, Jungle Boy and Luchasaurus finally captured tag gold ? Luchasaurus put Rey Fenix through a table at ringside before Jungle Boy sealed it with a pinning reversal on Penta El Zero Miedo, giving the team its first-ever title reign after over two years together.
It was 2022 when Malakai Black made their return to AEW television after 6 weeks away, appearing on Dynamite.
It was 2024 when Wheeler Yuta vs. Komander closed out Rampage, rated 6.35 in a hard-fought men's division clash.
